subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should it be a per-agent audited SSRF policy rather than a flat global `allowPrivateNetwork` key?
rationale: The code can already enforce private-network policy when passed through, but exposing it changes the SSRF trust boundary and requires a maintainer choice about authorization, metadata/link-local handling, redirects, and audit semantics.

options.title: Sponsor per-agent audited SSRF policy
options.body: Continue through the protected design/PR path with explicit requester authorization, audit output, cache-key isolation, and documentation before broad private-network access can land.

options.title: Reject arbitrary web_fetch private access
options.body: Keep `web_fetch` strict for arbitrary URLs and route trusted private workflows through narrower provider, browser, plugin, or explicit egress-policy surfaces.

options.title: Fold into broader egress policy
options.body: Defer this issue until the network allow/deny or interactive-confirmation design decides the permanent SSRF control model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor per-agent audited SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Continue through the protected design/PR path with explicit requester authorization, audit output, cache-key isolation, and documentation before broad private-network access can land.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the narrower fake-IP SSRF policy and explicitly framed this issue as the remaining security-sensitive config decision.
